Do not let the conversation migrate immediately to Revenue Model simply because it feels more practical or easier to prepare for. Once the Decision behaviour or structure is moving, strengthen Revenue Model so the original constraint is less likely to return.

Coaching sequence: Define ready enough before the next delay appears. Decide which conditions are genuinely necessary, set the action and timing, and use review points after movement rather than constant reconsideration before it. Then use the Secondary work to reinforce the change: Make the slow leakage visible, define the commercial threshold that requires change and implement one structural improvement before the business creates another reason to postpone it.

MORE_LEADS.text: The founder may believe stronger demand will make the business easier to move. If current opportunities are already stalling in Sales or Decision, more leads will simply create more open loops and more people waiting in the same process.
MORE_LEADS.diagnosticDirection: Likely first focus: Sales and/or Decision.

PRICE_TOO_HIGH.text: The founder may believe the market is not ready for the current price. If strong-fit prospects show interest but the founder delays increases, over-explains or waits for more proof before holding value, the issue may sit in Identity or Sales rather than in the number itself.
PRICE_TOO_HIGH.diagnosticDirection: Likely first focus: Identity and Sales.

NEW_OFFER.text: The founder may believe demand is inconsistent because the current offer is wrong. If the offer is already clear but promotion, follow-up or execution are inconsistent, rebuilding it can become another delay before the exposing commercial work happens.
NEW_OFFER.diagnosticDirection: Likely first focus: Decision and execution.

BETTER_SYSTEMS.text: The founder may believe operational improvement is the practical next step. If serious opportunities are not reaching a decision, stronger backend systems are unlikely to be the immediate commercial leverage point.

proposed.label: I need more time.
proposed.text: More time is useful only when it is expected to produce information, capacity or readiness that materially changes the decision. If the founder cannot name what will be different, the actual constraint may be Decision rather than timing.

proposed.label: The market is not ready yet.
proposed.text: The market may genuinely be early. It may also be receiving an unclear or inconsistent signal. If Positioning is weak, waiting for demand can postpone the very commitment required for demand to form.

proposed.label: My clients are not ready for a premium offer.
proposed.text: Some clients may not be ready. That does not prove none are. If the premium option does not exist, the business has no clean way to discover the demand or protect higher-value delivery commercially.

proposed.label: I need another few results before I raise my price.
proposed.text: Additional evidence can help. If existing outcomes, demand and experience already support a stronger position, the delay may be Identity rather than proof.

proposed.label: The business needs to settle before I fix the numbers.
proposed.text: A quieter period can make review easier. If the current Revenue Model is one reason the business never feels settled, waiting can simply extend the leakage.

proposed.label: The buyer needs more time.
proposed.text: Sometimes the buyer genuinely does. Sometimes they need a concern diagnosed, a clearer recommendation or a defined next step. Time should not be prescribed until the unresolved issue is understood.

proposed.label: I need more capacity before I grow.
proposed.text: Capacity can be a real constraint. The useful question is whether all capacity must exist before demand is tested, or whether a controlled commercial move can create the evidence and resources required to build it.

proposed.label: Now is not the right time.
proposed.text:
That may be correct. Ask what specifically makes the timing wrong, what must become true for it to become right and whether those conditions have a date, threshold or owner. If the answer remains vague, the statement may be protecting a Decision constraint.

SOURCE ANCHOR Book: Chapter One, The Revenue Illusion; Chapter Six, rhythm and revenue actions; Chapter Seven, leading the conversation; Framework: False Constraint examples and Constraint Engine.

riskSignals.label: Under-Claiming Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may be waiting for another level of experience or proof before claiming value the current evidence already supports.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Compare the stated readiness threshold with current results, demand and experience. Do not encourage a bigger claim without evidence, but do not let evidence move endlessly into the future.

riskSignals.label: Waiting-for-Demand Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may be expecting market demand to clarify a Positioning choice that the business itself needs to make first.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Define what evidence is already sufficient to choose and set a review period after commitment.

riskSignals.label: Premium Delay Risk
riskSignals.text: Higher-value client needs may exist without a structured premium offer because the founder believes demand or capacity is not ready enough.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Design a controlled next rung with clear scope and capacity boundaries, then test rather than assume demand.

riskSignals.label: Buyer-Readiness Risk
riskSignals.text: Prospects may be receiving more time than the decision actually requires.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Ask what remains unresolved and whether additional time is expected to change anything specific.

riskSignals.label: Slow Margin Leakage Risk
riskSignals.text: The Revenue Model may be tolerating weak economics because the business remains stable enough to keep operating.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Make the leak visible and connect it to Profit, owner value and Freedom before waiting for urgency.

riskSignals.label: Founder-Adaptation Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may be personally adapting around weak structures instead of changing them.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Identify where extra effort is keeping a weak model alive and choose one structural change.

riskSignals.label: Safe-Timing Risk
riskSignals.text: Important commercial moves may be waiting for conditions to feel safer than they need to be.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Define the minimum viable conditions for action before another delay appears.

riskSignals.label: Rhythm Risk
riskSignals.text: Revenue actions may still depend on workload, mood or timing rather than a protected weekly rhythm.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Pre-decide when the key commercial actions happen and review adherence, not intention.

riskSignals.label: Decision Drift Risk
riskSignals.text: Commercial decisions may remain open and repeatedly reconsidered without a clear expectation of new information.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Set the decision rule, date and review point. Do not keep the choice permanently live.

riskSignals.label: Capacity Gate Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may be treating current capacity as a reason not to test a commercial move that could itself justify building more capacity.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Separate capacity needed before a test from capacity required after proven demand.

IDENTITY.possibleLanguage: "I just need a little more experience or proof before I charge at that level."
IDENTITY.whatMaySitUnderneath: The statement may be reasonable. If Identity is constrained, the threshold may also be moving. Establish what evidence would genuinely make the stronger commercial position appropriate and whether that evidence already exists.
IDENTITY.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

POSITIONING.possibleLanguage: "I want to see where the market goes before I narrow this down."
POSITIONING.whatMaySitUnderneath: Market observation can be sensible. If Positioning is constrained, waiting may be creating the lack of clarity the founder is trying to solve. Ask what signal the market can realistically provide while the message remains broad or changeable.
POSITIONING.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

OFFER.possibleLanguage: "I do not think my clients are ready for the premium version yet."
OFFER.whatMaySitUnderneath: Some clients may not be. The question is whether this is known from a real offer test or assumed from current behaviour. If Offer is constrained, the business may be suppressing demand by never presenting a clear next level.
OFFER.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

SALES.possibleLanguage: "I do not want to push them before they are ready."
SALES.whatMaySitUnderneath: Respect for readiness is valuable. If Sales is constrained, the founder may be equating leadership with pressure. Ask what the buyer actually needs in order to decide and whether another period of waiting will provide it.
SALES.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

REVENUE_MODEL.possibleLanguage: "I want the business to settle down before I change the model."
REVENUE_MODEL.whatMaySitUnderneath: A quieter period may help, but the existing model may be contributing to why the business never feels settled. Make the cost of waiting visible and identify which change can be implemented without destabilising delivery.
REVENUE_MODEL.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

DECISION.possibleLanguage: "Now just is not the right time."
DECISION.whatMaySitUnderneath: That may be true. The useful question is what specifically makes the timing wrong, what needs to change, by when, and whether the founder has been moving that threshold each time conditions improve.
DECISION.responsePosture: Acknowledge the timing or practical concern first. Then connect it to the diagnostic evidence, ask what would genuinely change the decision and avoid responding with urgency before the real condition is understood. If the timing is genuinely wrong, respect that conclusion and define what a meaningful future review would require.

prosper.PERMISSION: Create an open beginning that gives the founder room to explain current reality, workload, context and what she believes makes the timing important. For a Timing-Led founder, acknowledgement of reality builds credibility. Permission also means giving yourself permission to lead once the conditions are understood.
prosper.REFRAME: Use the diagnostic to distinguish a genuine timing issue from the structural mechanism. The founder may believe the answer is more demand, more time, more capacity or a quieter period. Reframe towards the weak link and show which conditions matter before action and which can be built afterwards.
prosper.OWNERSHIP: Stand behind the diagnosis and recommendation without manufacturing urgency. A Timing-Led founder may look for a practical reason to wait. If the adviser continually adds preparation to keep the conversation comfortable, the conversation can reinforce the very pattern the diagnostic is trying to change.
prosper.STRUCTURE: Hold the shape of the conversation. Understand reality, diagnose the issue, explain the cost of waiting, define ready enough, make a recommendation and invite a decision. Do not allow practical discussion to become an endless list of conditions with no conclusion.
prosper.POWER_QUESTIONS: Ask questions that reveal what additional time is expected to create, which conditions are truly necessary, whether the threshold has moved before and what commercial cost is being created while the decision stays open. Ask, then listen.
prosper.EMBODIMENT: Remain calm when the founder says now is not the right time. Do not rush to contradict her. Help her define why, what must change and by when. Model the difference between respectful pacing and passive delay.
prosper.RESULT:
The conversation must arrive somewhere. State what you recommend, what the next step is and invite a clean yes, no or a genuinely defined not-yet. If the answer is not yet, the conditions and review point should be clear enough that the decision is not simply left open indefinitely.

ETHICAL TEST FROM THE BOOK Would this person thank you for the conversation in a year, whatever she decided in it? If yes, lead it clearly. If no, do not use profiling or urgency to force the sale.

SOURCE ANCHOR The Inevitable Standard Knowledge Base v1, Chapter Seven: Leading the Conversation. Key source ideas: Permission, Reframe, Ownership, Structure, Power Questions, Embodiment, Result, a clean yes or no and the ethical test for any sale.

preCall.intro: The adviser should prepare from the Quick Reference first, then use the deeper sections only where needed. Preparation should end with a hypothesis and a question, not a verdict. A useful pre-call review takes five to ten minutes and should answer the following in full sentences.
questions: What current condition does the founder appear to believe is most important to the decision?
What is the Primary Constraint and what evidence makes it higher leverage than the other weak areas?
What is the Secondary Constraint and how could it recreate the Primary pattern?
Which Green pillar can be used as leverage or evidence that the founder does not need to rebuild everything before moving?
What False Constraint may the founder bring into the call, and what evidence would help her see the distinction herself?
Which Timing-Led risk is supported by actual pillar states, and which stereotype is not supported?
What is the one decision this conversation should help the founder make?
What information, capacity or timing condition must genuinely be validated before recommending a next step?

IDENTITY: What evidence would make the next price or authority level appropriate?
Which of those conditions already exist?
How many times have you moved the threshold after reaching an earlier milestone?
What commercial move are you waiting to feel familiar before making?
What would happen if you treated current evidence as permission to test rather than as a requirement for total certainty?
POSITIONING: What market evidence are you waiting for before choosing?
Can the market produce that evidence while the message remains broad or keeps changing?
How long have you been testing the current alternatives?
What would a defined Positioning test period look like?
What would you choose if you knew you could review from evidence after ninety days rather than needing the permanent answer today?
OFFER: Which part of the next offer genuinely requires more capacity before testing?
What higher-value client need are you already meeting informally?
What would a controlled premium test look like?
What is the smallest commercial version that could create real demand evidence?
What are you assuming clients are not ready for without having offered it clearly?
SALES: When a buyer says they need more time, what do you normally ask next?
What do your buyers most often still need when the conversation stalls?
How long do you usually wait before following up?
What would a clear decision point look like without using pressure?
Which current opportunities already have enough information to decide?
REVENUE_MODEL: Which financial leak are you waiting for a quieter period to address?
What does that leak cost each month or quarter?
What has to be true before you change the pricing, margin or dependency structure?
Is the current model helping create the instability you want to wait out?
Which one change can happen without requiring the entire business to be settled first?
DECISION: What exactly needs to become true before you move?
What new information do you expect from waiting?
Who owns the condition and by when should it be met?
Have you added new requirements after earlier ones were satisfied?
If uncertainty never disappears completely, what would ready enough look like?

avoidedQuestion.IDENTITY: What if I am already ready enough to claim the value, and the thing I am actually waiting for is the feeling that the next level is familiar?
avoidedQuestion.POSITIONING: What if clearer demand is waiting for me to choose a clearer position first?
avoidedQuestion.OFFER: What if clients cannot show me they are ready for the premium offer because I have never given them a clear premium option?
avoidedQuestion.SALES: What if the buyer does not need more time and actually needs me to lead the decision more clearly?
avoidedQuestion.REVENUE_MODEL: What if the business is not going to settle until I change the structure I keep postponing?
avoidedQuestion.DECISION: What if the conditions are already sufficient and I am waiting for the discomfort of deciding to disappear?

challengeSequence.intro:
Challenge timing only after demonstrating that you understand the practical situation. If the founder has a real capacity, cash-flow, contractual or implementation constraint, acknowledge it. An adviser who dismisses reality will lose credibility and may push the founder towards a bad decision.

Once reality is understood, challenge the moving threshold. Ask what specific condition is missing, how the founder will know when it is met and what action follows. If the founder keeps adding new conditions, name the pattern carefully. The objective is to make readiness explicit, not to prove that every delay is avoidance.

Do not challenge ambition, prudence or sustainable pace as though they are problems. Do not use behavioural profiling to tell the founder what she secretly feels. Do not challenge a genuine financial constraint as though it is a mindset issue. The commercial evidence and live conversation must remain primary.

buyingResistance.buying:
The founder starts asking how the intervention would fit current commitments, what happens first, what can wait and how quickly a specific part could be implemented. She begins defining the conditions for movement rather than speaking about timing generally. She asks about sequence, capacity, milestones, review points or how to start without disrupting delivery. These may indicate that the buying decision is becoming practical rather than hypothetical.

Do not treat operational questions as resistance automatically. For Timing-Led buyers, implementation questions can be strong engagement signals. The adviser should notice whether the questions are converging towards a decision or expanding indefinitely.
buyingResistance.resistance:
The founder repeatedly says not yet without defining what must change. Each resolved condition creates another requirement. The conversation keeps moving into preparation, future quarters or hypothetical scenarios. She wants more time but cannot say what new information that time will provide. She becomes more interested in making the decision safer than in determining whether the recommendation is actually right.

Resistance signals are hypotheses, not proof. A new legitimate constraint may have emerged. Ask before interpreting.

nextStepPositioning.IDENTITY: Position the intervention as helping the founder bring commercial value into line with evidence already present, using controlled actions to create the next layer of confidence rather than waiting for familiarity first.
nextStepPositioning.POSITIONING: Position the intervention as converting good market awareness into one clear signal, with a defined test period and review point so the founder does not need permanent certainty before choosing.
nextStepPositioning.OFFER: Position the intervention as creating the next sensible client rung within clear delivery limits, allowing real market evidence to replace assumptions about whether buyers are ready.
nextStepPositioning.SALES: Position the intervention as keeping respectful buyer pacing while adding clearer diagnosis, recommendation, follow-up and decision points so more time is used only when it genuinely improves the decision.
nextStepPositioning.REVENUE_MODEL: Position the intervention as identifying and repairing slow leakage before it becomes urgent, protecting stability while improving margin, repeat value, owner benefit and reduced founder dependency.
nextStepPositioning.DECISION:
Position the intervention as defining ready enough, setting practical thresholds and dates, and turning good judgement into a protected rhythm of action rather than repeated reconsideration.

OFFER-FIT BOUNDARY Do not infer a recommended package or spending level from Timing-Led style alone. Use diagnosed need, readiness, explicit business context, implementation capacity and the actual offer criteria.

C.followUp:
Timing-Led follow-up should be calm, specific and decision-relevant. Summarise what you heard, the diagnosed constraint, why it matters now, the recommendation and the timing condition that remains open. If the founder genuinely needs time, define what the time is expected to produce and when the decision should be reviewed.

If additional information is required, send only what addresses the decision-relevant gap. Avoid overwhelming the founder with extra preparation that creates more conditions to assess. If the founder asks for another conversation, agree what that conversation is intended to resolve. The follow-up should model the same principle the report teaches: practical pacing with a clear destination.

postSaleCoaching.intro:
Once the founder becomes a client, the report shifts from selling support to coaching guidance. The priority remains the same: work the Primary Constraint first, use Green pillars as leverage, strengthen the Secondary Constraint so the pattern does not return and prevent readiness from becoming a moving requirement each time the agreed action approaches.

Timing-Led coaching should create evidence through controlled movement. Practise the price change, offer test, follow-up rhythm, financial review or leadership decision, then review what actually happened rather than what the founder predicted might happen. The founder should never feel that caution is being punished. The coach is helping her distinguish thoughtful pacing from commercial drift.

Where useful, pre-decide the action. Put it in the calendar. Define what would genuinely stop it. Review the result afterwards. This follows the book's emphasis on rhythm, repeated revenue actions and making standards into decisions held in advance rather than choices renegotiated every day.

byState.GREEN: Use light accountability. Confirm the pillar remains healthy and redirect coaching energy to the constraint. Ask the founder to use the Green strength actively, for example using strong Decision to implement an Offer test or strong Revenue Model to support a deliberate pricing move.
byState.AMBER: Use stabilising accountability. Identify the situations in which readiness changes, agree one or two explicit thresholds or behaviours and review them in real commercial situations. The aim is consistency, not speed for its own sake.
byState.RED: Use focused accountability. Define the missing condition, decide whether it is genuinely necessary, schedule the action and review the evidence. The founder may bring credible practical reasons to delay. The coach should keep returning to the binding constraint until the evidence changes or a genuine external condition requires the plan to change.

progressSignals.IDENTITY: The founder states price and authority closer to the level current evidence supports, stops moving the proof threshold automatically and takes visible commercial actions before the new level feels completely familiar.
progressSignals.POSITIONING: The market position becomes clearer, testing has a defined review period, message changes are driven by meaningful evidence and the founder stops waiting for demand to make the strategic choice on her behalf.
progressSignals.OFFER: A clear entry, core and premium pathway exists, higher-value needs are commercialised rather than handled informally and the founder tests new offer levels within defined delivery limits.
progressSignals.SALES: Buyer hesitation is diagnosed rather than automatically given more time, recommendations become clearer, follow-up happens on a defined rhythm and sales cycles shorten without artificial pressure.
progressSignals.REVENUE_MODEL: Slow leakage is identified and reduced, pricing and margin decisions happen before crisis, repeat value becomes clearer and founder dependency begins to reduce instead of being tolerated as the price of stability.
progressSignals.DECISION:
The founder defines ready enough, sets dates and thresholds, reduces repeated reconsideration and moves important commercial actions while some uncertainty still remains.

SOURCE ANCHOR Book anchors: Chapter Four on identity evidence through action; Chapter Five on structure, offer, price and client pathway; Chapter Six on revenue actions and rhythm; Chapter Seven on clear sales decisions; Chapter Nine on standards as decisions held in advance.

adviserFlags.green: The founder can name the real practical condition and decide whether it matters. She can distinguish current capacity from future capacity that can be built. She uses dates and thresholds rather than a general sense of not yet. She is willing to test reversible decisions. Sales follow-up happens on a rhythm. Financial changes occur before crisis. Green pillars are treated as foundations rather than reasons to create more work.
adviserFlags.red:
Every approaching commercial action creates another readiness condition. The founder repeatedly says the business must settle, the market must clarify or the buyer needs more time without defining what will change. High-value work stays informal because the premium option is always a future project. Financial leakage is accepted because it remains manageable. The coach finds herself helping the founder prepare indefinitely rather than helping her move.

A Red Flag is not a reason to refuse service automatically. It is a prompt for stronger diagnosis, clearer scope, more explicit expectations or, where appropriate, referral to another qualified professional if the issue sits outside the adviser's competence.

coreProfile.whatApproachMeansInternally:
An Evidence-Led founder naturally gives meaningful weight to proof, numbers, logic, systems, process and commercial defensibility. She is often less persuaded by confidence alone and more interested in whether the recommendation can be explained, tested and supported. That rigour can be commercially valuable because it helps protect margin, quality, process and decision quality when other founders may move mainly from instinct.

This founder may be strong at financial clarity, quality control, operational design, commercial modelling and identifying risk. She can be the person who asks what the numbers actually say while everybody else is reacting to enthusiasm or fear. In a mature expression, Evidence-Led judgement creates disciplined decisions and a business that understands why its economics work.

The risk is not evidence itself. The risk is allowing the proof standard to expand until certainty becomes the requirement. Another case study, another comparison, another scenario, another model or another round of analysis can feel commercially responsible while the action that would create the most useful new evidence remains unmade.

The adviser therefore needs to distinguish diligence from avoidance and useful analysis from delayed ownership. The question is not whether more information could be gathered. It is whether that information is likely to change the decision. If the founder cannot say what new evidence would alter the answer, the analysis itself deserves investigation.

EVIDENCE-LED INTERNAL RULE Keep the proof. Define what is sufficient. Make the decision when the evidence is decision-ready, then let action create the next layer of evidence.
coreProfile.whatTheyNaturallyNotice:
Evidence-Led founders often notice gaps in logic, missing numbers, process risk, inconsistencies, margins, assumptions, scope, quality standards and whether a commercial claim is defensible. They may quickly identify where another person is making a leap that has not been supported, and they often want to understand the mechanism beneath an outcome rather than accepting a confident promise at face value.

That awareness is useful when it improves the decision. It becomes costly when every unanswered question is treated as equally important. The adviser should keep separating decision-critical evidence from interesting detail, reversible risk from irreversible risk and proof that must exist before action from proof that can only be created after action begins.
coreProfile.whatMotivatesThem:
Evidence-Led founders are often motivated by commercial coherence. They want the pieces to make sense together. They may engage strongly when they can see how the recommendation connects to the numbers, what mechanism is expected to create the outcome, what assumptions sit underneath the plan and how progress will be measured. Competence and precision often build confidence more effectively than enthusiasm alone.

Do not mistake this for a lack of ambition or emotion. Many Evidence-Led founders care deeply about the future and the people around the decision. They simply want the claim to survive scrutiny. A strong adviser respects that instinct while preventing the conversation from becoming an unlimited exercise in removing uncertainty that cannot realistically be removed in advance.
coreProfile.behaviourUnderPressure:
Under pressure, Evidence-Led strength can become cognitive expansion. The founder may respond to uncertainty by gathering more data, building more scenarios, asking more questions or redesigning the system. That activity can look highly productive and still delay the commercial action the evidence already supports.

Pressure can also increase over-explanation. When a buyer hesitates, the founder adds proof. When a price feels exposed, she builds a more detailed justification. When a model underperforms, she improves the dashboard. The coach should not remove the value of evidence. The coach should keep asking which decision the evidence is meant to inform and whether that decision has actually been made.

SOURCE ANCHOR Framework: Evidence-Led moves through data, proof, systems, process, risk, numbers and logic. Book: diagnosis before prescription; confidence follows action; work the weak link; rhythm beats intensity; Revenue -> Profit -> Personal Wealth -> Freedom.
coreProfile.howTheyThink:
Evidence-Led thinking begins with what can be supported. The founder is likely to notice the facts, numbers, process, assumptions, risk and whether the commercial story survives scrutiny. She tends to value internal consistency and may want to understand how one part of the recommendation causes another rather than simply being told that the outcome is possible.

This can make her unusually disciplined. She may be good at spotting weak margin, identifying where an offer cannot scale, noticing inconsistencies in buyer data or challenging a plan whose economics are not yet clear. She can also create repeatable delivery because she cares about process and quality rather than leaving every result to individual judgement.

The risk is assuming that every missing piece of information deserves to be solved before movement. Some proof is only created because the price was quoted, the offer was released, the market position was held or the decision was implemented. The adviser should help the founder classify evidence into three groups: required before action, useful but not decisive, and only learnable after action.

The Green, Amber and Red pillar results determine where this thinking style is currently helping or hurting. If Revenue Model is Green, analytical rigour may already be protecting the economics. If Revenue Model is Red, measurement may exist without action. If Decision is Green, the founder can recognise sufficient evidence. If Decision is Red, certainty may have become the gate.
coreProfile.howTheyDecide:
Evidence-Led founders often decide by asking whether the commercial case makes sense. They may consider the numbers, alternatives, scope, process, risk, assumptions and whether the expected outcome is supported. This can protect the business from impulsive movement and from recommendations built mainly on confidence or social pressure.

The central risk is allowing a good evidence question to become an endless evidence question. The strongest decision process defines what evidence matters and what threshold is sufficient. Once that threshold is met, the founder moves. When Decision is Amber or Red, the coach should look for the proof requirement expanding after earlier questions have already been answered.

A useful distinction is between information and certainty. More analysis is justified when it can materially change the choice. More analysis is less useful when it is primarily expected to remove the normal discomfort of committing while some uncertainty remains. The adviser should ask what exact evidence would change the answer and whether that evidence is obtainable before action.

DECISION RULE Define sufficient evidence before collecting more. If the decision-critical threshold is met, decide, act and review from new evidence afterwards.
coreProfile.howTheyBuy:
Evidence-Led founders are likely to evaluate whether the recommendation is commercially coherent, not simply whether the outcome sounds attractive. They want to understand the problem diagnosis, why the proposed intervention fits it, what process is involved, what evidence supports the recommendation and what risk remains. This means the adviser should be prepared to explain the commercial logic rather than relying on charisma or urgency.

A strong buying conversation gives enough evidence to support the decision without turning the call into a research project. State what is known, what is inferred and what remains uncertain. Show the mechanism, scope and next step. Then ask what information is still decision-critical. This protects the founder's need for rigour while preventing the proof requirement from expanding indefinitely.

Buying behaviour must still be qualified by the actual scores. An Evidence-Led founder with Green Decision may make a clear decision after asking detailed questions. Those questions are not automatically hesitation. A founder with Red Decision may keep requesting more material after the decision is already adequately supported. A founder with Red Revenue Model may have a legitimate commercial affordability issue. Do not interpret every request for evidence as avoidance.

The internal standard is informed clarity, not information pressure. A good adviser can accept that the current evidence is genuinely insufficient while still requiring a precise answer about what is missing, why it matters and how the decision will be revisited. That protects buyer agency and prevents an indefinite maybe from being disguised as due diligence.

SOURCE ANCHOR QSC reference: how they buy, decide, what communication lands, trust requirements and blockers. Inevitable Standard adaptation: qualify all guidance with actual pillar and constraint evidence.
coreProfile.priceAndValue:
Do not infer spending power or a maximum price from an Evidence-Led result. The useful prediction concerns the way commercial value is evaluated. This founder is likely to want the investment to make logical sense in relation to the problem, expected outcome, scope, alternatives and risk. A price presented without a commercial case can feel arbitrary, even when the amount itself is affordable.

The adviser should connect price to the diagnosed constraint and the value of changing it. Where possible, use the founder's own numbers, costs, conversion, margin, time or opportunity data rather than generic return-on-investment claims. Be transparent about what can and cannot be quantified. Evidence-Led trust falls quickly when a calculation looks inflated or when assumptions are hidden.

The pillar pattern changes the interpretation. Identity Red may mean the founder applies a harsher proof standard to investing in herself than she applies to other business decisions. Revenue Model Red may indicate a genuine need to understand cash flow, margin or affordability before proceeding. Decision Red may mean pricing questions continue after the commercial case is already sufficiently clear. Validate which issue is actually present.

PRICE BOUNDARY Do not convert behavioural style into a predicted budget or pricing tolerance. Use explicit business context, diagnosed need, affordability information supplied by the founder and the configured offer criteria.
coreProfile.trustBuilders:
Evidence-Led trust is strengthened by competence, consistency and intellectual honesty. The adviser should be able to explain why the diagnosis was reached, which evidence supports it, where the limits of the assessment are and how the recommendation connects to the actual commercial issue. A confident admission that something is not yet known can build more trust than pretending certainty.

Specificity matters. Use the founder's own results. Refer to the exact pillar pattern. Distinguish Primary from Secondary Constraint. Show how a Green pillar acts as leverage. If a False Constraint is being challenged, show why the alternative explanation fits the evidence better rather than simply telling the founder she is wrong.

Process also matters. Explain what happens next, what the intervention will and will not cover, what evidence of progress will be tracked and when decisions will be reviewed. Evidence-Led founders often trust an adviser more when the work has a clear reasoning structure and accountability loop.
coreProfile.trustReducers:
Unsupported claims, vague inspiration, overconfident promises, inconsistent numbers, changing logic, hidden assumptions and generic recommendations can reduce trust quickly. So can becoming defensive when the founder asks detailed questions. Questions may be part of how she validates competence rather than a sign that she is resisting the conversation.

The opposite problem also matters. An adviser who responds to every question with another document, case study or fifteen-minute explanation can accidentally reinforce the founder's belief that complete proof is possible before action. Answer precisely, then ask whether the information changed the decision and what remains unresolved.

Do not weaponise the profile. Telling the founder that she is over-analysing simply because she asks for evidence will damage trust and weaken the diagnostic. Use the actual Decision, Sales or relevant pillar evidence before challenging the proof requirement.
coreProfile.communicationStyle:
Communication should be structured, specific and commercially relevant. Begin with the diagnosis and why it matters. Explain the logic. Use the minimum evidence required to support the recommendation. Make assumptions explicit. Then bring the conversation back to the decision rather than allowing detail to expand without purpose.

A useful order is: commercial problem, evidence, consequence, recommendation, relevant proof, next step. This avoids two common failures. The first is leading with vague inspiration that never establishes credibility. The second is leading with so much methodology that the founder loses the commercial meaning of the recommendation.

Use precise language without becoming overly technical. Where the founder asks for detail, answer the question directly and check whether it is decision-critical. The best communication does not make the founder feel less intelligent. It makes the decision easier to see.
coreProfile.coachingStyle:
Evidence-Led coaching should honour rigour while creating movement. The coach should not tell the founder to ignore the numbers, stop thinking or act on instinct. The work is to define which evidence matters, what threshold is sufficient and what can only be learned through action. This preserves the strength of the approach instead of treating it as a defect.

Make accountability observable. If the coaching conversation produces analysis, attach it to a decision. If a metric is reviewed, identify what action the metric is meant to trigger. If more research is requested, define the question it must answer and the date on which the decision returns. This prevents intelligent preparation from becoming an endless substitute for exposure to the market.

Use Green pillars actively. If Decision is Green, remind the founder that she already knows how to recognise sufficient evidence and move. If Revenue Model is Green, use the strength of the economics to support Identity or Offer work. The coaching goal is not to improve everything. It is to use the strongest existing structure to repair the highest-leverage constraint.

FUTURE_LED.intro: A Future-Led secondary influence adds possibility, ambition and strategic imagination to the Evidence-Led core. This can be powerful because the founder can see where the business could go and wants a credible commercial case underneath it. The risk is oscillation between a bold future and a proof standard that no genuinely new opportunity can fully satisfy in advance, or selectively using evidence to support an opportunity she already wants to be true.
FUTURE_LED.buyingImplication: Lead with the future value, then give the commercial case, assumptions and evidence that matter. Do not model every possible outcome. Define the minimum proof required to test the opportunity safely and show how the first stage creates new evidence.
FUTURE_LED.coachingImplication: Use future possibility to create movement and evidence to create discipline. Separate assumptions from facts, define the test and stop the founder from turning strategic modelling into a substitute for market evidence.

CONNECTION_LED.intro: A Connection-Led secondary influence adds people, trust and relational impact to the Evidence-Led core. This founder may be excellent at translating complexity into a conversation people can understand. The tension appears when she wants the other person to feel completely convinced, which can lead to over-explaining, or when a strong relationship makes uncomfortable evidence harder to act on.
CONNECTION_LED.buyingImplication: Build personal credibility as well as the commercial case. Explain the logic in human language, connect evidence to the founder's actual situation and allow questions. Then check what she genuinely needs to understand to decide rather than trying to remove all relational discomfort through more proof.
CONNECTION_LED.coachingImplication: Help her distinguish explanation from reassurance. Use evidence to support clear conversations with clients and team, but keep decision ownership visible when the numbers and the relationship point in different directions.

TIMING_LED.intro: A Timing-Led secondary influence adds readiness, context and practical capacity to the Evidence-Led core. This can create excellent risk control and operational judgement. The risk is a double movement threshold: Evidence wants enough proof and Timing wants the conditions to be right, so the founder can keep increasing the amount of certainty required before action is allowed.
TIMING_LED.buyingImplication: Provide the decision-critical evidence and a realistic implementation path. Then define what conditions genuinely need to exist now and what can be built during the work. Ask what new evidence or condition would actually change the answer before granting more time.
TIMING_LED.coachingImplication: Set evidence thresholds and readiness thresholds in advance. Once both are met, move. Use review points after action instead of allowing a new round of proof and timing conditions to reopen the decision.

BALANCED.intro: Evidence-Led remains clearly dominant, but no single secondary influence consistently controls the supporting decision process. Context will determine whether future value, people or timing becomes the second filter. Proof remains the anchor, so the adviser should listen for which additional condition the founder believes must be satisfied before the evidence can become action.
BALANCED.buyingImplication: Start with the commercial logic and then ask what else matters to the decision. The answer will reveal whether the active supporting filter is future value, relationship confidence or implementation timing. Keep the evidence requirement tied to a defined decision rule.
BALANCED.coachingImplication: Keep the Evidence-Led core central. Define sufficient evidence first, then use live questioning to identify the secondary filter before challenging the remaining hesitation.

IDENTITY_GREEN.pillarMasterIntro:
Identity measures whether the founder can hold the commercial weight of the business when value becomes visible, priced and asked for. It includes pricing belief, commercial authority, visibility, willingness to ask, tolerance for a no and steadiness under price pressure.

Evidence-Led Identity naturally claims authority through proof, competence, results and defensible reasoning. The strength is credibility. The risk is requiring more proof than the market or the decision genuinely needs, so expertise keeps accumulating while price, visibility and authority remain one step behind.
IDENTITY_GREEN.commercialRoleInSystem: The main commercial exposures associated with a weak Identity result include underpricing, unnecessary discounting, weak visibility, indirect asking, over-education and a gap between capability and what the business actually earns. The Revenue-To-Freedom links most directly affected are Revenue and Profit. These are commercial consequences, not predictions of personal financial outcomes.
IDENTITY_GREEN.approachCoachingPrinciple: Define what evidence is sufficient to support the commercial claim. Once that threshold is met, act and let market response create the next layer of proof rather than collecting evidence indefinitely.
IDENTITY_GREEN.whatThisResultTellsYou: This pillar is currently operating with enough structure and repeatability to be used as leverage. Do not manufacture an Evidence-Led problem simply because the approach has known risks. Green evidence shows where proof, logic and rigour are already supporting commercially dependable behaviour. The founder uses evidence to ground authority without making certainty a prerequisite. She can state the value, make the offer, remain visible and allow real market response to create the next layer of proof. The evidence supports the commercial claim rather than delaying it.
IDENTITY_GREEN.howThisAffectsThinking: In Identity, the founder is currently able to use proof, logic and structure without allowing analysis to overwhelm the commercial standard. Use this as evidence that Evidence-Led thinking itself is not the problem here. The useful question is how this strength can support the Primary Constraint and reduce the temptation to rebuild an area that is already holding.
IDENTITY_GREEN.howThisAffectsDeciding: A Green result suggests the founder can use evidence without surrendering commercial ownership in this area. Do not assume Evidence-Led means slow or analytical here. The evidence says she currently recognises when enough is known and can move. Define what evidence is sufficient to support the commercial claim. Once that threshold is met, act and let market response create the next layer of proof rather than collecting evidence indefinitely.
IDENTITY_GREEN.howThisAffectsBuying:
When buying support in this area, the founder is likely to value a clear commercial case, credible process and evidence of fit, but the Green result suggests she can decide without eliminating every uncertainty. Give her the relevant proof, explain the logic and invite a decision.

Connect the work to observable behaviour such as price holding, visibility, asking and margin rather than vague confidence language.

strongestPillar.IDENTITY: Use strong Identity as evidence that this founder can ground authority in proof and still make the commercial claim. If Sales or Decision is constrained, do not send her back into more credentials, case studies or authority-building work. Use the existing steadiness to support a clearer ask or faster decision.
strongestPillar.POSITIONING: Use strong Positioning to show that evidence is already being translated into buyer recognition. If Sales is weak, the right people may already understand the business. Do not solve the wrong problem by adding more research or technical messaging.
strongestPillar.OFFER: Use strong Offer as evidence that rigour is already producing a clear commercial product. If Sales or Decision is weak, the founder does not need another round of design before leading the buyer or making the next decision.
strongestPillar.SALES: Use strong Sales to show that this founder can use proof selectively and still lead a buyer to a decision. If another pillar is weak, avoid assuming more evidence, more detail or more sales process is automatically the answer.
strongestPillar.REVENUE_MODEL: Use strong Revenue Model as evidence that the founder can translate numbers into sound economics. If Identity or Decision is weak, use those economics to support the commercial claim or action rather than producing another financial model.
strongestPillar.DECISION: Use strong Decision to challenge any stereotype that Evidence-Led automatically means analysis paralysis. This founder can recognise sufficient evidence and move. Use that strength to address the actual Primary Constraint with a defined action and review point.

IDENTITY.whatIsReallyHappening: The founder is not consistently claiming commercial value at the level the current expertise, results or market evidence may already support.
IDENTITY.approachMechanism: Evidence-Led can amplify this when the founder treats proof as permission. Another result, credential, case study or level of certainty becomes a reason the price, authority or visibility should wait.
IDENTITY.commercialCost: Watch for underpricing, unnecessary discounting, weak visibility, indirect asking, over-education and a gap between capability and what the business actually earns.
IDENTITY.conversationObjective: Help her establish a reasonable evidence threshold for the commercial claim, compare it with what already exists and identify the visible action that should happen once the threshold is met.
IDENTITY.coachingPriority: Define what evidence is sufficient to support the commercial claim. Once that threshold is met, act and let market response create the next layer of proof rather than collecting evidence indefinitely.
IDENTITY.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I just need a little more proof before I charge at that level." The objection may be legitimate diligence, but if Identity is constrained the proof threshold may be functioning as permission. Ask what evidence would make the stronger price commercially defensible and whether that evidence already exists.

SOURCE ANCHOR Chapter Two, The Identity Gap; Chapter Four, Becoming the Prosperity Architect; Chapter Six, Running the Machine; Appendix B, Founder's Playbook.

POSITIONING.whatIsReallyHappening: The market signal is not clear enough for the right people to recognise themselves quickly and understand why the business matters.
POSITIONING.approachMechanism: Evidence-Led can make the position highly specific yet too technical. The founder may explain the mechanism or proof more clearly than the buyer problem, urgency and outcome.
POSITIONING.commercialCost: Watch for mixed-fit leads, long explanations, lower category distinction, greater price comparison and too much reliance on the founder personally creating relevance.
POSITIONING.conversationObjective: Translate the evidence into buyer meaning. Help her identify the one audience, commercial problem and distinction the market needs to recognise before the detailed proof is introduced.
POSITIONING.coachingPriority: Keep the precision and proof, then translate them into buyer recognition. Lead with the commercial problem, who it matters to and the outcome before the methodology, data or proof stack.
POSITIONING.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I need to refine the message because people still do not fully understand it." The founder may need refinement, or the message may be carrying too much technical explanation. Ask whether the buyer fails to understand the mechanism or fails to recognise why the problem matters to them.

SOURCE ANCHOR Chapter One, The Revenue Illusion; Chapter Three, The Three Revenue Breakdowns; Chapter Five, Building the Machine.

OFFER.whatIsReallyHappening: The expertise is not packaged in a commercial structure clear enough to buy, price, deliver and repeat consistently.
OFFER.approachMechanism: Evidence-Led can overbuild the product. The founder may keep adding detail, options, process and edge-case logic because completeness feels commercially responsible, while the buyer-facing decision becomes harder.
OFFER.commercialCost: Watch for scope drift, inconsistent pricing, weak margin, bespoke delivery, lack of a premium path and too much founder judgement required in every engagement.
OFFER.conversationObjective: Protect the internal rigour while simplifying the purchase. Help her define the outcome, scope, price and client path in the fewest components required for a confident decision.
OFFER.coachingPriority: Keep the structural rigour behind the scenes and simplify the buyer-facing decision. Name the outcome, define the scope, price with margin and use a clear entry, core and premium pathway rather than explaining every internal mechanism.
OFFER.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I want to make the offer more complete before I sell it." Completeness can improve delivery, but an Evidence-Led founder can overbuild before testing. Clarify the minimum structure required for a confident purchase and what can be learned through a controlled first version.

SOURCE ANCHOR Chapter Five, Building the Machine, especially Sell a product, not an afternoon, the three-rung ladder, price logic and the client pathway.

SALES.whatIsReallyHappening: Real opportunity is reaching the business, but too little of it is becoming a clear commercial decision.
SALES.approachMechanism: Evidence-Led can respond to buyer uncertainty with more evidence rather than more leadership. Proof, detail and explanation can become substitutes for recommendation, asking and closing the loop.
SALES.commercialCost: Watch for warm leads, good conversations, open maybes, inconsistent follow-up, weak recommendation and lower conversion than the level of interest suggests should be possible.
SALES.conversationObjective: Diagnose what the buyer actually needs to decide, present only the relevant proof and then move clearly into recommendation, investment and decision.
SALES.coachingPriority: Diagnose first. Present only the proof that resolves the buyer's actual concern. Then make a clear recommendation, state the investment, ask for the decision and close the follow-up loop.
SALES.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I need to give them more information before I ask." The buyer may genuinely need information. If Sales is constrained, more proof may also be replacing the commercial recommendation. Ask what question remains unanswered and whether the buyer has actually requested more evidence.

REVENUE_MODEL.whatIsReallyHappening: The business is creating money but not retaining, repeating or transferring enough of the value it creates.

REVENUE_MODEL.commercialCost: Watch for weak margin, old pricing, low owner pay, constant reinvestment, lack of repeat purchase and founder dependency.
REVENUE_MODEL.conversationObjective: Make the decision threshold explicit. Identify what the numbers already support, choose the commercial change and agree how the result will be reviewed after implementation rather than modelled indefinitely beforehand.
REVENUE_MODEL.coachingPriority: Set decision thresholds around the numbers. When the commercial case is sufficient, implement the pricing, margin, retention or dependency change and review the result later rather than trying to model every outcome first.
REVENUE_MODEL.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I want to run the numbers a bit more before I change anything." Further modelling can be valuable, but if the decision would remain the same across reasonable scenarios, analysis may no longer be the limiting factor. Define the threshold that would change the action.

DECISION.whatIsReallyHappening: The business may already know what needs to happen, but important commercial actions are not becoming decisions and follow-through quickly enough.
DECISION.approachMechanism: Evidence-Led can mistake certainty for readiness. The founder may keep collecting information because another data point could reduce uncertainty, even when the remaining uncertainty is not decision-critical.
DECISION.commercialCost: Watch for open loops, repeated rebuilding, delayed pricing, weak follow-up, safe preparation and strategic drift.
DECISION.conversationObjective: Define what evidence would genuinely change the answer. If that evidence is already present, make the decision, agree the action and move the review point to after implementation.
DECISION.coachingPriority: Define what evidence would genuinely change the answer. When the remaining uncertainty is not decision-critical, decide, act and use the result as new evidence. Protect a review rhythm rather than continuous reconsideration.
DECISION.likelyBuyingObjectionTheme:
"I am not certain enough yet." Certainty is rarely available in commercial decisions. The useful question is what uncertainty remains, whether it is material and what evidence would genuinely change the answer.
