MORE_LEADS.text: If enquiries already exist but conversion, follow-up or clean decisions are weak, lead volume is not the first fix. More opportunity can simply make the existing leak larger. An Evidence-Led founder may be attracted to more acquisition data, funnel analysis or channel optimisation because those activities feel measurable. Bring attention back to what happens to the leads already present.

PRICE_TOO_HIGH.text: If strong-fit prospects show interest while the founder discounts, over-explains, adds scope or hesitates to hold the price, the number itself has not yet been tested cleanly. Evidence-Led founders can build elaborate price justification when the more useful intervention is stronger Identity and Sales behaviour.

NEW_OFFER.text: If the offer is already understandable but promotion, follow-up or execution are inconsistent, rebuilding it can become another round of design and analysis. The business may need Decision and execution to stabilise before another product model is created.

BETTER_SYSTEMS.text: Systems may be useful later, but if Revenue is low because sales conversations are not reaching decisions, additional backend complexity is not the first fix. This False Constraint can be especially attractive to an Evidence-Led founder because systems and process are natural strengths.

proposed.label: "I need more data."
proposed.text: More data is useful only when it could genuinely change the decision. Ask which data point would alter the recommendation, what threshold would matter and whether that information already exists. If the answer would remain the same, Decision may be the stronger constraint.

proposed.label: "I need to prove the value more clearly."
proposed.text: The buyer may already have enough proof. If the conversation keeps expanding rather than reaching a recommendation, Sales may be the stronger constraint. The question is whether another proof point will resolve a real buyer concern or simply delay the ask.

proposed.label: "I need a more complete system first."
proposed.text: Additional system detail can feel commercially responsible while delaying a market test. Offer or Decision may need a simpler first move so the business can create evidence through real use rather than through continued design.

proposed.label: "I cannot raise the price until the model is perfect."
proposed.text: Pricing should be commercially defensible, but perfection is not the threshold. Identity and Revenue Model may already provide enough evidence for action. Set the price decision from current value, margin and market evidence, then review from response.

proposed.label: "I need to compare a few more options."
proposed.text: Comparison is useful when the options differ on a decision-critical dimension. If the criteria are already clear and one route fits them, more comparison can become a way of postponing commitment rather than improving judgement.

proposed.label: "I need to reduce the risk first."
proposed.text: Some risks should be reduced before movement. Others are only discoverable through controlled action. Clarify which risk is material, how it can be bounded and whether the first step can be designed as a test rather than requiring complete certainty.

riskSignals.label: Proof Threshold Risk
riskSignals.text: The amount of proof required before claiming authority or making a commercial move may be higher than the decision genuinely needs.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Define sufficient proof in advance and act once the threshold is met.

riskSignals.label: Technical Positioning Risk
riskSignals.text: The business may explain method, logic or evidence more clearly than why the problem matters to the buyer.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Translate proof into buyer language: problem, consequence, outcome and distinction first.

riskSignals.label: Complexity Risk
riskSignals.text: The offer or process may contain more detail than the buyer needs to make a confident decision. Internal rigour should not create external friction.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Simplify the buyer-facing decision while keeping the internal operating logic intact.

riskSignals.label: Over-Explanation Risk
riskSignals.text: Proof may be used after the buyer already has enough information. More explanation can delay the recommendation and direct ask.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Answer the question that is actually present, then return to the decision.

riskSignals.label: Analysis-to-Action Risk
riskSignals.text: Commercial data is being gathered or modelled without a sufficiently clear trigger for action.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Attach a decision rule and action threshold to the analysis before more data is collected.

riskSignals.label: Certainty Risk
riskSignals.text: Decisions may wait for confidence that no realistic business decision can provide in advance.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Define the uncertainty that matters, bound it and move when the remaining unknowns are not decision-critical.

riskSignals.label: Metric-Hiding Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may be using measurement as a substitute for confronting the commercial behaviour the numbers already reveal.
riskSignals.adviserResponse: Ask which decision the metric is meant to inform and whether that decision has actually been made.

riskSignals.label: Proof-Before-Ask Risk
riskSignals.text: The founder may believe the buyer needs another explanation, case study or model before a direct commercial ask is appropriate.
riskSignals.adviserResponse:
Test whether the buyer has asked for more proof. If not, make the recommendation and invite the decision.

RISK-FLAG RULE Do not infer a risk flag solely because the founder is Evidence-Led. The underlying answers must support it. Use no more than the signals that materially help the next conversation.

IDENTITY.possibleLanguage: "I just need a little more proof before I charge at that level."
IDENTITY.whatMaySitUnderneath: The objection may be legitimate diligence, but if Identity is constrained the proof threshold may be functioning as permission. Ask what evidence would make the stronger price commercially defensible and whether that evidence already exists.

POSITIONING.possibleLanguage: "I need to refine the message because people still do not fully understand it."
POSITIONING.whatMaySitUnderneath: The founder may need refinement, or the message may be carrying too much technical explanation. Ask whether the buyer fails to understand the mechanism or fails to recognise why the problem matters to them.

OFFER.possibleLanguage: "I want to make the offer more complete before I sell it."
OFFER.whatMaySitUnderneath: Completeness can improve delivery, but an Evidence-Led founder can overbuild before testing. Clarify the minimum structure required for a confident purchase and what can be learned through a controlled first version.

SALES.possibleLanguage: "I need to give them more information before I ask."
SALES.whatMaySitUnderneath: The buyer may genuinely need information. If Sales is constrained, more proof may also be replacing the commercial recommendation. Ask what question remains unanswered and whether the buyer has actually requested more evidence.

REVENUE_MODEL.possibleLanguage: "I want to run the numbers a bit more before I change anything."
REVENUE_MODEL.whatMaySitUnderneath: Further modelling can be valuable, but if the decision would remain the same across reasonable scenarios, analysis may no longer be the limiting factor. Define the threshold that would change the action.

DECISION.whatMaySitUnderneath: Certainty is rarely available in commercial decisions. The useful question is what uncertainty remains, whether it is material and what evidence would genuinely change the answer.

prosper.PERMISSION: Set the purpose and boundaries of the conversation. Explain that you will use the diagnostic as evidence, ask questions to validate what is true and make a recommendation only if the result and the conversation support it. This lowers the need for the founder to defend every assumption immediately.
prosper.REFRAME: Use the False Constraint where relevant. Show the founder how the visible problem differs from the structural issue and use her own scores or examples to make the distinction. The reframe should feel more evidentially coherent, not merely more persuasive.
prosper.OWNERSHIP: Stand behind the diagnosis and recommendation without pretending certainty. An Evidence-Led founder may test the logic carefully. If the adviser becomes vague or keeps adding proof instead of holding the recommendation, the conversation can reinforce the very pattern the diagnostic is trying to change.
prosper.STRUCTURE: Explain the relevant sequence: Primary first, Secondary next, Green leverage and the specific commercial consequence. Evidence-Led trust increases when the path has a reason and when the adviser can explain why other possible improvements are not first.
prosper.POWER_QUESTIONS: Ask questions that expose whether more proof is genuinely required, which assumption matters, what the founder already knows and what action the current evidence supports. Questions should create better evidence rather than simply invite more analysis.
prosper.EMBODIMENT: Model the behaviour being recommended. Be precise, calm and transparent. Answer the question, name uncertainty where it exists, make the recommendation and do not hide behind unnecessary complexity.
prosper.RESULT:
Lead to a clean yes, no or defined not-yet. A not-yet should specify what evidence is missing, why it matters, how it will be obtained and when the decision returns. An undefined maybe is not a decision process.

SOURCE ANCHOR The book's seven-part conversation structure: Permission, Reframe, Ownership, Structure, Power Questions, Embodiment, Result. Use it as an ethical conversation architecture, not a persuasion script.

questions: Which evidence is genuinely decision-critical for this conversation and which detail can wait?
What is the Primary Constraint and what evidence makes it higher leverage than the other weak areas?
What is the Secondary Constraint and how could it recreate the Primary pattern?
Which Green pillar can be used as leverage or proof that the founder does not need to rebuild everything?
What False Constraint may the founder bring into the call, and what evidence would help her see the distinction herself?
Which Evidence-Led risk is supported by actual pillar states, and which stereotype is not supported?
What is the one decision this conversation should help the founder make?
What assumption in your own recommendation should you be ready to explain or revise if the founder provides better information?

IDENTITY: What evidence currently supports the value you are creating?
What additional proof do you believe you need before changing price, visibility or authority?
Would that evidence genuinely change the commercial case, or mainly change how comfortable the claim feels?
Where is your current commercial position still reflecting an earlier version of your capability?
What would you do differently this month if you accepted that the evidence was already sufficient?
POSITIONING: What does the right buyer need to recognise before they care how your method works?
Where does your message become technical before commercial relevance is established?
What market evidence is decision-critical and what research is merely interesting?
Which audience and problem create the clearest commercial case today?
What would you remove from the first explanation if the buyer only had thirty seconds?
OFFER: What outcome is the buyer actually purchasing?
Which parts of the current offer are essential to that outcome and which exist because the internal model is detailed?
Where does complexity make pricing, scope or delivery harder?
What is the simplest credible entry, core and premium pathway?
What could be tested with real clients rather than modelled internally for another month?
SALES: What question is the buyer actually trying to answer before deciding?
What proof is genuinely relevant to that question?
Where do you tend to explain beyond the point the buyer needs?
What recommendation would you make if you were not trying to remove every uncertainty first?
What would a clean yes, no or defined next step look like at the end of the conversation?
REVENUE_MODEL: Which number is currently telling you something needs to change?
What decision is that number meant to inform?
What threshold would justify changing price, margin, retention or founder involvement?
Is additional modelling likely to change the action?
How will you review the result after implementation rather than trying to predict every outcome first?
DECISION: What evidence would genuinely change this decision?
Which remaining unknown is materially decision-critical?
What can be learned only after action?
Is this decision reversible enough to test rather than prove completely?
What date or threshold marks the point where analysis ends and action begins?

avoidedQuestion.IDENTITY: "What if the evidence is already enough and the real risk is continuing to price, present or hide yourself as though it is not?"
avoidedQuestion.POSITIONING: "What if the buyer does not need more information and simply cannot recognise why this matters quickly enough?"
avoidedQuestion.OFFER: "What if making the offer more complete is actually making the decision harder to buy?"
avoidedQuestion.SALES: "What if the buyer already has enough proof and the missing step is your recommendation and ask?"
avoidedQuestion.REVENUE_MODEL: "What if the numbers are already clear and the analysis is now protecting you from implementing the decision?"
avoidedQuestion.DECISION: "What if no additional information will remove the uncertainty you are waiting to remove?"

challengeSequence.intro: Evidence-Led founders may be very capable of defending their reasoning. A useful challenge therefore needs to be precise. Do not challenge intelligence, diligence or the desire for evidence. Challenge the decision rule, the relevance of the evidence, the cost of complexity or the point where analysis stops improving the commercial outcome.

byPillar.IDENTITY:
Challenge whether additional proof would genuinely change the commercial claim or merely make it feel safer. Ask what evidence threshold would make the price or authority defensible, then compare that threshold with what already exists.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.
byPillar.POSITIONING:
Challenge whether the market needs more technical explanation or a simpler statement of the problem, consequence and outcome. Ask what the right buyer should recognise in the first thirty seconds before any methodology is explained.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.
byPillar.OFFER:
Challenge whether complexity is serving delivery or protecting the founder from releasing a simpler commercial decision into the market. Ask which components are essential to the outcome and which exist mainly because the internal model can accommodate them.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.
byPillar.SALES:
Challenge whether the buyer has actually asked for more proof. Ask what remains unresolved, make the recommendation and test whether the founder is using explanation to avoid the exposing moment of asking.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.
byPillar.REVENUE_MODEL:
Challenge whether additional analysis would change the decision. If the numbers already support a pricing, margin, retention or dependency move, ask what is stopping implementation and move the review point to after action.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.
byPillar.DECISION:
Challenge certainty directly but respectfully. Ask what evidence would change the answer, whether that evidence is obtainable before action and whether the remaining uncertainty can be bounded through a reversible test.

Do not challenge this too early if the relevant pillar evidence is Green, if a material fact is genuinely missing or if the founder has identified a specific piece of information that could change the decision. Validate before interpreting.

buyingResistance.buying:
The founder starts asking implementation questions, wants to understand how the first stage works, tests the recommendation against her own numbers, begins discussing what would need to change operationally, asks about measurement or review points, or identifies what evidence would confirm the intervention is working. These can indicate movement because the questions are converging towards execution rather than expanding the decision space.

Another strong signal is when the founder begins summarising the logic herself: "So the real issue is Sales, not more leads," or "The numbers already support the price change." That suggests the diagnosis has become internally coherent. The adviser should still ask for the decision rather than assuming intellectual agreement equals purchase commitment.
buyingResistance.resistance:
The founder repeatedly asks for new categories of proof after earlier questions have been answered, keeps comparing options without a stable criterion, shifts the decision to a new metric each time the current metric supports movement, requests extensive detail that would not change the recommendation or becomes more focused on proving the adviser wrong than understanding the commercial issue. These signals deserve curiosity rather than pressure.

Do not treat operational or financial questions as resistance automatically. For Evidence-Led buyers, rigorous questions can be strong engagement signals. The adviser should notice whether the questions are converging towards a decision or expanding indefinitely.

nextStepPositioning.IDENTITY: Position the next step around converting existing proof into commercial authority: stronger price holding, visible value claims, direct asks and evidence created through action. Do not sell more confidence in the abstract.
nextStepPositioning.POSITIONING: Position the next step around turning research and specificity into buyer recognition. The value is not more information. It is a clear market signal that the right people understand quickly.
nextStepPositioning.OFFER: Position the next step around simplifying and productising the expertise while protecting scope, margin and the client pathway. Make simplicity feel like disciplined design rather than loss of rigour.
nextStepPositioning.SALES: Position the next step around using proof more selectively and strengthening diagnosis, recommendation, asking and follow-up. The buyer should understand that the intervention improves commercial leadership, not merely presentation quality.
nextStepPositioning.REVENUE_MODEL: Position the next step around converting financial visibility into implemented economics: margin, pricing, repeat value, owner value and reduced founder dependency. Include decision thresholds and review points.
nextStepPositioning.DECISION:
Position the next step around defining sufficient evidence, creating decision rules and protecting a rhythm of action and review. The value is not certainty. It is better movement under real-world uncertainty.

OFFER-FIT BOUNDARY Do not infer a recommended package or spending level from Evidence-Led style alone. Use diagnosed need, readiness, explicit business context, implementation capacity and the actual offer criteria.

D.followUp:
Evidence-Led follow-up should be concise, structured and decision-relevant. Summarise what you heard, the diagnosed constraint, the evidence that supports it, the recommendation, the decision or open question and the next agreed step. Do not automatically attach every available case study, deck or document. Send only material connected to a question that genuinely remains open.

If the founder needs more information, agree what question the information is expected to answer and when the decision returns. If the founder needs time, define what will be different after the time. The follow-up should preserve buyer agency while stopping analysis from becoming unbounded.

postSaleCoaching.intro: Once the founder becomes a client, the same internal intelligence should support coaching. The coach should use the Priority Fix Order rather than allowing the founder to redirect attention towards the most interesting model, metric or framework. Evidence-Led founders may be especially capable of creating sophisticated work around a secondary issue while the Primary Constraint remains exposed.

byPillar.IDENTITY:
Define what evidence is sufficient to support the commercial claim. Once that threshold is met, act and let market response create the next layer of proof rather than collecting evidence indefinitely.

Use the strongest Green pillar as evidence and leverage. Make the next commercial action observable, attach any analysis to a decision rule and agree the review point before more data is collected.
byPillar.POSITIONING:
Keep the precision and proof, then translate them into buyer recognition. Lead with the commercial problem, who it matters to and the outcome before the methodology, data or proof stack.

Use the strongest Green pillar as evidence and leverage. Make the next commercial action observable, attach any analysis to a decision rule and agree the review point before more data is collected.
byPillar.OFFER:
Keep the structural rigour behind the scenes and simplify the buyer-facing decision. Name the outcome, define the scope, price with margin and use a clear entry, core and premium pathway rather than explaining every internal mechanism.

Use the strongest Green pillar as evidence and leverage. Make the next commercial action observable, attach any analysis to a decision rule and agree the review point before more data is collected.
byPillar.SALES:
Diagnose first. Present only the proof that resolves the buyer's actual concern. Then make a clear recommendation, state the investment, ask for the decision and close the follow-up loop.

Use the strongest Green pillar as evidence and leverage. Make the next commercial action observable, attach any analysis to a decision rule and agree the review point before more data is collected.
byPillar.REVENUE_MODEL:
Set decision thresholds around the numbers. When the commercial case is sufficient, implement the pricing, margin, retention or dependency change and review the result later rather than trying to model every outcome first.

byPillar.DECISION:
Define what evidence would genuinely change the answer. When the remaining uncertainty is not decision-critical, decide, act and use the result as new evidence. Protect a review rhythm rather than continuous reconsideration.

byPillar.IDENTITY: Track the visible commercial claim, not more preparation. Did the price get stated? Was the offer made? Was the authority claim published? What happened in the market after action?
byPillar.POSITIONING: Set a defined message and review window. Do not let new research alter the live position until the agreed evidence threshold or review date is reached.
byPillar.OFFER: Lock the buyer-facing structure for a defined test period. Route new ideas and edge cases into a version backlog unless evidence shows they are necessary to the current outcome.
byPillar.SALES: Track conversations started, recommendations made, offers stated, decisions asked for and follow-ups completed. Do not count additional decks, case studies or explanatory material as a substitute for commercial movement.
byPillar.REVENUE_MODEL: Attach actions to metrics. If margin falls below the threshold, what changes? If a client remains on old pricing, by when is it reviewed? If founder dependency exceeds the target, what responsibility moves next?
byPillar.DECISION:
Use decision logs with the evidence required, the decision date, the action, the review date and what would justify reversal. Prevent continuous re-analysis between the decision and the review point.

ACCOUNTABILITY PRINCIPLE Every important analysis should answer: Which decision does this inform, what threshold matters, what action follows and when will the result be reviewed?

progressSignals.IDENTITY: The founder states price and authority closer to the level current evidence supports, stops moving the proof threshold automatically and creates new commercial evidence through visible action.
progressSignals.POSITIONING: The message becomes easier for the buyer to recognise, technical detail moves later in the communication sequence and lead fit improves without the founder personally explaining the whole methodology.
progressSignals.OFFER: The buyer-facing offer becomes simpler, scope and margin remain protected, the client pathway is clear and internal complexity no longer makes the purchase harder than necessary.
progressSignals.SALES: The founder diagnoses before explaining, uses proof selectively, makes clearer recommendations, asks directly and closes follow-up loops instead of sending more material by default.
progressSignals.REVENUE_MODEL: Financial analysis produces implemented pricing, margin, repeat-value and dependency decisions. Fewer dashboards remain disconnected from action and owner value becomes more explicit.
progressSignals.DECISION: The founder defines decision criteria in advance, stops collecting information that would not change the answer and uses post-action review to create the next layer of evidence.

adviserFlags.green: The founder can explain what evidence matters to the decision and what does not. Questions become more specific and converge towards implementation. She is willing to make a decision with explicitly bounded uncertainty. Green pillars are accepted as strengths instead of being reopened for more optimisation. The Primary Constraint remains the centre of the work even when more interesting analytical projects appear. Metrics and analysis are linked to actions, thresholds and review dates. The founder can change her mind when new evidence genuinely contradicts the original assumption without treating every new data point as a reason to reopen everything.
adviserFlags.red: Every answer produces another category of evidence that must be gathered before movement. The founder asks for more detail without being able to explain what decision the detail will change. The conversation becomes more technical while the commercial problem becomes less clear. Offer, Positioning or systems are repeatedly rebuilt even though the Primary Constraint sits elsewhere. Financial analysis is sophisticated but pricing, margin or owner-value decisions remain unimplemented. The founder uses the profile to justify avoiding uncertainty rather than to understand her decision process. The issue moves into regulated financial, legal, tax, clinical or other professional territory outside the adviser's competence.
